finance_aml.gbm.baseline_gap_note: This reaches minority-class F1 well below the published 0.6323 (GFP+XGBoost, AMLworld HI-Small, NeurIPS 2023 D&B). The cause is a feature ARCHITECTURE difference, not a tuning one: the gap is unreachable at any threshold, because measured AUPRC is far below what that F1 requires. IBM's Graph Feature Preprocessor computes per-transaction subgraph patterns over a dynamically updated graph; this project computes per-account scalar aggregates. A degree is one number per account, whereas a GFP feature is a pattern match in that transaction's own neighbourhood at the moment it arrives. GFP ships in `snapml` under a Proprietary licence and is excluded by this project's commercial-OK-only rule, but the licence is not itself the cause - the architecture is, and it is reimplementable without `snapml`, simply at more cost than renaming aggregates. Reachability is computed to 4 hops against injected CYCLE attempts of up to 10; that was previously recorded as a main cause and is NOT one - the GFP paper (arXiv:2402.08593) decomposes its own contribution, and its Table 5 (HI-Small, XGBoost, batch 128) gives fan-in/fan-out, which this project approximates with per-account aggregates, 37 F1 points (19.75 to 56.88) and multi-hop cycle and scatter-gather patterns 1.7 more (to 58.60; 'up to 4%' in its text is F1 points, not a relative gain). The evaluation is strictly inductive and temporally split. Per-account aggregates are causal (each row sees only edges strictly before it); the structural block - cycle closure, scatter-gather, bank diversity, burst degree - is still fitted on the training window, because recomputing sparse reachability at every timestep is not tractable here. Reported as measured; not adjusted to close the gap. Full workings: references/finance-gap-investigation.md.

calibration.does_not_move_ranking: Platt is STRICTLY monotone, so AUC and AUC-PR are unchanged by construction: measured Round 49, both are identical to the uncalibrated values to ten decimals, and that held for the map fitted on the probability and for the logit(s) map that now ships alike. The qualifier matters and was missing - isotonic is only WEAKLY monotone, and on this same split it moved AUROC by -0.00031674 and AUPRC by -0.01121590 (-9.09%). Calibration by a strictly monotone map fixes what a probability MEANS, never how the rows are ordered. ONE HONEST QUALIFIER ON THE MAP THAT SHIPS: logit() clips at 1e-12, so scores below 1e-12 or above 1-1e-12 would tie. None exist on this split (the raw range is 4.4e-11 to 0.99997), so no pair is tied and the AUCs above are exact; a retrain that saturates a leaf would need this re-checked rather than assumed.
calibration.fitted_on: validation split; scored on the held-out test split
calibration.formula: p = 1 / (1 + exp(a * logit(clip(score, logit_clip_eps, 1 - logit_clip_eps)) + b)), logit(q) = log(q / (1 - q))
calibration.reliability_diagram_defensible_here: YES on the test split, which carries 2,321 events. Van Calster et al. (J Clin Epidemiol 2016) ask for at least 200 events and 200 non-events before a flexible calibration curve, and Riley et al. (Stat Med 2021) show that such rules of thumb can still be too few. NO on the browser's evaluation sample: 8,192 rows from the same test window at a 0.02 base rate, so 164 events, which is why the page draws no curve and says so. Each number is right for its own denominator, and confusing the two is the mistake this repository documents under 'ask what the metric was divided by'. The floor also binds on medical (42 events) and satellite (113). The CORP terms below are reported regardless, because PAV picks no bin count and so they are stable where a binned curve is not.
calibration.why_not_isotonic: MEASURED Round 49 on this split, not argued: isotonic Brier 0.00142218 / log-loss 0.00820025 against 0.00142199 / 0.00818964 for the same fit_platt fed logit(s) - within noise on both proper scoring rules, so ICML 2005's 'as good as, or better than' holds here in the 'as good as' form. Platt is kept on the tie-break: isotonic is only WEAKLY monotone, collapsed 1,388,669 distinct scores to 138, and cost AUROC 0.00031674 and AUPRC 0.01121590 (-9.09%), while both Platt arms moved neither to ten decimals; it also emitted exactly 0 on 464,176 test rows, one a true positive, and 138 breakpoints are not two floats a browser can apply. ONE CORRECTION TO THE OLD REASONING SURVIVES HERE: the calibration set carries 801 events, not 2,321 (that is the test split). The second - that a/b were fitted on a PROBABILITY rather than a log-odds, making the map return 0.00090148 for nine of ten deciles - is FIXED, not outstanding: on_logit is true above and the map published here is the logit(s) arm those numbers describe. Workings: references/finance-calibration-isotonic-vs-platt.md.

finance_aml.scorecard.metric_note: Fitted by maximising net benefit across five decision thresholds rather than a surrogate loss. `fit_method` is 'coordinate-search': the objective it maximises is the exact AUNBC, but optimality is NOT claimed - the exact integer program over all (sample x threshold) indicators is not tractable at this row count, and reporting a heuristic's result as an optimum would be a different claim. `exact_under_bfv` records that the encrypted score equals the plaintext score bit for bit, which is the property a CKKS student cannot offer; verified in tests/test_scorecard_bfv_exact.py.

calibration.argument: the student's P(laundering), $q = \sigma(w^\top z + c)$, where $w^\top z + c$ is the decision logit the encrypted path decrypts, $z$ the z-scored features and $c$ the student's intercept (`b` in its weights file). The tuned threshold is folded into $c$, so the operating point is $q = 0.5$, a logit of 0

Isotonic's Brier 0.00149696 is below Platt's 0.00154002 and its log-loss 0.00837343 is below 0.00864886; lower is better on both. Platt is kept as a choice, not as the better score: it is strictly monotone, so the curve ranks rows as the student does (AUPRC 0.02410110 against the raw 0.02410110, with 168 test rows tied at the logit clip; isotonic's 0.02459877 comes from the test window's scores tied at 109 values, 207,340 of them exactly zero), and it is the teacher's method, so the page's two decision curves differ by the model and not by the map. scripts/measure_decision_curve.py records the student's window curve under both maps.

not_measured.published_source: PGS Catalog PPM002038 for PGS000072: AUROC 0.637 (no confidence interval recorded), incident breast cancer in n=216,273 European-ancestry women in UK Biobank - 4,760 cases and 211,513 controls - from Kachuri et al., Nat Commun 11:6084 (2020), doi:10.1038/s41467-020-19600-4. A CITATION AND NOT A TARGET, for three reasons the record itself gives: the model is fitted WITH COVARIATES (age at assessment, family history of breast cancer, genotyping array, PCs 1-15, parity, age at menarche, body mass index, menopausal status, hormone replacement therapy, oral contraceptive use, alcohol intake, and body mass index by menopausal status), which a bare weighted dot product does not have; it used 'only 162 of the original 187 SNPs'; and it is an AUC at 5 years. It is the only AUROC among the score's three Catalog performance records; the other two report an odds ratio per standard deviation of 1.26 (95% CI 1.24-1.28; PPM000192, GERA and UK Biobank, n=237,549, Graff et al. 2021) and a hazard ratio of 1.26 (1.20-1.32; PPM017165, post-menopausal breast cancer, UK Biobank, n=1,990; Byrne et al., Int J Epidemiol 52:817-826, 2023).
not_measured.reason: 1000 Genomes is a reference panel with no breast-cancer case/control status. AUROC requires a phenotyped cohort, so the published figure is carried as a citation, not as a measurement from this run: 0.637 (AUROC (European ancestry)).

medical_fl.student.baseline_gap_note: This scores far below the 0.901 ResNet-18 baseline. The reason is representational rather than cryptographic: 3,226 parameters over a 14x14 input is a REPRESENTATION choice, not a feasibility limit - and this note said 'a CKKS-feasibility budget' until Round 32, which overstated how forced it was. Kim et al. (arXiv:2506.15258) do HE chest-X-ray inference on a VQGAN latent at downsampling factor 8 rather than on pixels, so the alternative to downsampling 28->14 is re-representing the input. The browser already runs onnxruntime-web, so such an encoder would run locally in plaintext with no privacy loss. Recorded as the sixth falsifiable trigger in the additional-model decision in docs/deliverable-verification.md, not acted on - and note that f=8 on a 28x28 input gives 3.5x3.5, so the transfer is the open measurement rather than a citation. This sentence claimed the trigger existed for two rounds while the table held five rows and none of them was this one; the trigger was written, and the decision moved to a tracked file so the claim can be checked. Round 24 found it had been WORSE than that - a constant predictor, emitting one class for all 156 test images, with accuracy 0.730769 exactly equal to the majority-class rate and AUC 0.354, below random. It was invisible because the registry declared `auc` while the record stored `accuracy`, and because this student had neither protection its teacher already had: class-weighted loss and AUC-based model selection. Both were added. Read `n_classes_predicted` and `majority_class_rate` beside the score - an accuracy equal to the majority rate is the signature of a model that learned nothing. Workings: references/medical-student-collapse-investigation.md.
medical_fl.student.metric_note: Two metrics are recorded and they answer different questions. `auc` is the registry's declared headline and is what the published baseline compares against. `student_metric`/`teacher_metric` are accuracy, because fidelity compares DECISIONS and a decision has no score to rank - so agreement and metric_delta are necessarily computed on a decision metric. Do not read the accuracy against the AUC baseline.

satellite_comms.telemanom.baseline_gap_note: Read n_events_scored before comparing this to the baseline. Since Round 86 the forecaster follows ESA-ADB's Telemanom-ESA recipe on its own Mission1 split: a 30 s zero-order hold, training only on unlabelled windows before 2007-01-01 with early stopping on the months from 2006-10-01, a 10-step forecast scored on its first step, and Telemanom's thresholding per channel. The half after the split holds 29 labelled anomalies of the 51 on these channels. This score is the plain zero-order hold at an error floor of 0.0105 raw units, chosen on the validation months, which hold 2 anomalies: tp=23 fp=0 fn=6, 8,069 of 7,364,160 points flagged. The published 0.968 is Telemanom-ESA-Pruned, whose floor of 0.05/7 the paper does not show was chosen without the test half, and it is scored on ESA-ADB's prepared series, which writes annotated samples the zero-order hold dropped back onto the grid - a step that reads the labels. Replicating both gives 0.968 (tp=25 fp=0 fn=4), and 0.791 over all events but communication gaps, where Table 2 prints 0.786 (28 of 65 events here; the published recall 0.424 is no whole number of events out of this count, so ESA-ADB's all-events set differs from this selection by at least one event); esa_scores holds every arm and floor. Remaining differences: PyTorch where ESA-ADB uses Keras, from Keras's initialisers, one seed, and ESA-ADB's per-file resampling at the split. Until Round 86 this model trained at 300 s on a 70/30 cut holding 3 events and flagged 2 of 441,600 points. Workings: references/satellite-event-count-investigation.md.

satellite_comms.telemanom.metric_note: ESA-ADB's event-wise F0.5 for anomalies alone, scored by a reimplementation of its ESAScores: an anomaly is detected when any flagged event intersects it, and a flagged event is a false positive only when it intersects no annotated event of any category. corrected_event_wise_f0_5 multiplies event precision by the time-level true-negative rate, as ESA-ADB reports it; event_wise_f0_5 does not. Telemanom's paper prints 0.71 under F0.5 in its Table 2, though its own precision and recall there (87.5% and 80.0% overall) give 0.86. point_adjusted_f1 is shown only to expose how much point adjustment inflates: Kim et al. (AAAI 2022) show that under point adjustment even a random anomaly score can reach state-of-the-art. Only labels whose ESA-ADB Category is 'Anomaly' count as positives; the 63 rare nominal events annotated on these six channels do not.
satellite_comms.telemanom.sample_size_note: Read n_events_scored before comparing this to a published figure. The denominator of an event-wise metric is EVENTS: 29 anomalies in this test half, so one event either way moves the score by a visible step. n_anomaly_intervals counts label ROWS, one per channel an anomaly touches (320); n_anomaly_events_timeline counts the anomalies themselves (51). The number is reported as measured rather than reweighted, with the sample size beside it so the comparison is not made silently.

telecom_ids.nidd.baseline_gap_note: There is no baseline number to have a gap to, and that is a deliberate registry decision rather than a missing measurement: the two figures usually quoted for this corpus (99.61% for a classical CNN, 99.71% for a hybrid quantum-classical Quan-ConvCNN, Wang/Fok/Thing) are ACCURACIES on the BINARY benign-versus-malicious task, and this model is judged on 9-class macro F1, so putting them in `baseline` would render an accuracy beside a macro F1 as though the two were the same scale. WHAT THE COMPARISON CAN AND CANNOT SAY. This model scores about 0.7616 9-class accuracy with every row identifier, every host fingerprint and the file label dropped. The 9-class anchors are the dataset paper's random forest at 99.48% accuracy on its top-10 features (Samarakoon et al., arXiv:2212.01298) and BiTAD (Future Internet 17(11) 482) at 0.9047; this model sits below them, on its own stratified random split rather than a shared one, so each is an anchor and not a head-to-head. WHAT THE COUNTERFACTUALS SHOW. Restoring the corpus's integer row counters takes accuracy to about 0.9997, recorded every run as `leak_counterfactual_accuracy`, and restoring the file label to about 0.9829, recorded as `file_label_counterfactual`: that is what a bookkeeping column is worth on this corpus. They do not show what the published figures used. Whether the published figures lean on such columns is OPEN: the dataset paper's top-10 inputs include the sequence number `Seq` and `Offset`, Wang/Fok/Thing's inputs include `Offset`, both columns are dropped here, and no published ablation settles it.

capture_time_counterfactual.what_this_means: `IdleTime` holds 17 values, all multiples of 128, the spacing of a 32-bit float at this size. As Unix times they fall between 13 and 15 September 2022, and each is dominated by one attack scenario and benign traffic, so the column reads as when a flow was captured, the reason the loader drops `StartTime`. Restoring it lifts accuracy by about 22 points. That gain is a model learning when each attack was run, and none of it is a flow statistic. The shipped model does not read it.

carried_forward_not_remeasured.note: These fields were NOT measured by the run that wrote this record. They were inherited from the previous one because this run did not produce them - usually an optional stage that was skipped. Read them as measurements of the run named in measured_at_git_sha, not of this record's own git_sha. Re-run the stage that produces them to refresh, or delete them deliberately if the model no longer emits them; either way the change is then visible in the diff rather than silent.

export.int8_skipped_reason: tree ensemble: parameters live in node attributes, not weight tensors, so dynamic int8 quantisation has nothing to quantise

file_label_counterfactual.what_this_means: `IdleTime` holds 17 values, all multiples of 128, the spacing of a 32-bit float at this size, one for each attack session and base station. Read as Unix times they fall between 13 and 15 September 2022, and the dataset paper gives the captures as 26 and 29 August 2022, so the column does not measure anything about the flow: it names the file the flow came from, and each file is one attack. Restoring it lifts accuracy by about 22 points. That gain is a model recognising the file, and none of it is a flow statistic. The shipped model does not read it.

telecom_ids.nidd.framing: Real 5G network traffic, 9 attack classes, 46 flow-statistic features. This is a NETWORK-LAYER model and a different task from the QKD-layer classifier on the same page - no shared labels, no shared features, so the two scores are not a comparison. UNTIL ROUND 86 THIS MODEL ALSO READ `IdleTime` AND SCORED ACCURACY 0.9829. That column names the attack-session file a flow came from, not anything the flow did, so the model was recognising the file; it no longer reads it, and accuracy is 0.7616. Four numbers are recorded beside the headline and each is worth more than the headline. `file_label_counterfactual` restores that column and `leak_counterfactual_accuracy` restores four integer row counters, and each takes accuracy to 0.98 or above, which is not a better model but a leak. `flow_level_ceiling` is about 0.7685, the most any model reading these 46 columns could score, because whole feature vectors occur under both Benign and UDPFlood. And `cross_base_station` trains on one base station and tests on the other, where accuracy falls to about 0.42 and 0.61: the random split behind the headline flatters it.

idle_time_ablation.what_this_means: Removing `IdleTime` ALONE costs essentially the same accuracy as removing all six columns Combined.csv omits, and both land on the score this model published while it was fitted on Combined.csv. The other five - `Dir`, `Flgs`, `TcpOpt`, `sVlan`, `dVlan` - are worth 0.0006 accuracy between them. So the model's former weakness was one absent flow statistic, not the corpus and not the method. THAT IS REDUNDANCY AND NOT EMPTINESS, stated because the shorter version would be false. Two of those five are individually strong - `Dir` scores one-vs-rest AUC 0.9811 on ICMPFlood and `TcpOpt` 0.9433 on SlowrateDoS, both above the 0.90 threshold `single_feature_leak_check` uses, and both appear in its flagged list. What the ablation shows is that the other 41 columns already carry what they carry. `IdleTime` IS NOT AN IDENTIFIER and the distinction is the same one `leak_counterfactual_*` exists to draw: it takes 17 distinct integer values over 1,215,890 rows, so it cannot encode a row position, and it separates `SlowrateDoS` - an attack defined by holding a connection idle - at one-vs-rest AUC 0.9574. A row counter that scores that well describes where a row sits in a file. This describes what the traffic did.

linear_baseline.what_it_is: multinomial logistic regression on the 37 NUMERIC features only, standardised, fitted directly rather than distilled. The 10 ordinal codes are excluded because their integer order is nominal and a linear model would read it as a magnitude. Recorded as the classical floor and as a feasibility probe for a future CKKS-linear tier: it predicts 9 of 9 classes, so a linear student on this corpus does not collapse the way an 8-class one nearly does elsewhere in this project.

telecom_ids.nidd.metric_note: THE TWO NUMBERS READ THE OPPOSITE WAY ROUND FROM EVERY OTHER MODEL IN THIS PROJECT. Everywhere else here the aggregate flatters and the per-class figure exposes it, which is why `aggregate_accuracy` is rendered as the companion 'shown so the gap is visible'. On this corpus macro F1 is the OPTIMISTIC number and aggregate accuracy the PESSIMISTIC one: 0.9275 against 0.7616. THE MECHANISM, which is the part a reader is most likely to get wrong. It is not that a small class drags the macro average - the smallest class, ICMPFlood at 289 test rows, scores 1.0000 and lifts it. Benign at 39.3% of rows and UDPFlood at 37.6% are the only pair that confuses at all, they carry 77% of the test set between them, so accuracy is dominated by them while a macro average over 9 classes is carried by the seven scoring 0.9875 or better. Read `per_class_f1` and it is visible directly: the two lowest entries are Benign at 0.6401 and UDPFlood at 0.7308, and every other class is at or above 0.9875. A linear model on the numeric columns reaches accuracy 0.7549, so on this split the trees add little on those two classes. Neither figure is the flattering one to quote alone.
telecom_ids.nidd.sample_size_note: Trained and scored on the whole of 5G-NIDD BTS1_BTS2_fields_preserved.csv - 1,215,890 flows, stratified 75/25 at seed 42, so the test split is 303,973 rows and every class keeps its corpus proportion. Row for row this is the same corpus as Combined.csv, which this model used until Round 50; only the column count differs, 113 against 52. No subsampling and no class rebalancing: `ICMPFlood` is 1,155 rows in the corpus and 289 in the test split, which is small but is the real prevalence, and resampling it would report a per-class F1 for a distribution the deployed model never sees. The browser evaluation sample is a different matter and is NOT proportional - see the note in eval_sample.json, which states its per-class floor and why its macro F1 is not this one.

single_feature_leak_check.what_this_means: One-vs-rest rank-AUC per feature per class, at the 0.90 threshold scripts/prep_model_inputs.py already publishes against, measured AFTER all 66 drops. A LARGE NUMBER HERE IS EXPECTED ON THIS CORPUS AND IS NOT THE LEAK THIS MODEL IS ABOUT. The attacks are generated by distinct tools against distinct services, so a scan, a SYN flood and a slow-rate HTTP attack genuinely differ in TTL, packet rate, TCP window and ACK timing - these are the flow statistics an intrusion detector is supposed to use. The check's own docstring anticipates the case and warns rather than failing. The distinction that matters is against `leak_counterfactual_*`: `Unnamed: 0`, `Rank`, `Seq` and `Offset` cleared the same threshold while being bookkeeping columns that carry no information about the traffic at all, which is why those four are dropped and these are kept. The check cannot tell a file label from a statistic: `IdleTime` is out because its values name the attack session's file, which only reading the values showed, and `file_label_counterfactual` records what it was worth. Recorded rather than described so the distinction is checkable.

telecom_ids.qml.classical_rf_attribution_note: Impurity importance (training split, biased toward high-cardinality features) and permutation importance (held-out split, scored on macro F1, 20 repeats, std reported). Read the permutation figure where they disagree. These rank which features of a SYNTHETIC corpus this forest needs, not signals from a real QKD link. Two planted features are nearly redundant: sift_ratio separates detector_blinding perfectly on its own yet costs almost nothing to remove, because click_asymmetry separates the same class; and dark_count_rate is within one std of zero. Exact linear SHAP does not apply to a tree ensemble, which is why these two measures are used instead.

telecom_ids.qml.dataset: QKD attack telemetry (synthetic, signatures of this project's own design)

telecom_ids.qml.framing: Architecture comparison, not a performance claim. The published model is the random forest; the quantum-kernel SVC and the variational QNN are recorded beside it and not published. The data is synthetic because no commercial-OK real QKD-attack corpus exists. Published QML-IDS results are mixed rather than uniformly below a random forest: Al-Kuwari et al. (arXiv:2509.14282) report a hybrid QLSTM at 94.7% against their own random forest, while arXiv:2512.05069 was withdrawn by its own authors for insufficient evaluation. Per-class F1 is the headline; aggregate accuracy is shown beside it because Engelen et al. (WTMC 2021) demonstrated it stays at 0.99 across a label correction that moved Bot F1 from 0.60 to 0.99.

quantum_comparison_like_for_like.basis: binary attack-against-normal macro F1, each quantum model against a forest trained and scored on that model's own split and labels

telecom_ids.student.argmax_location: client, in plaintext, after decrypting all 8 class scores
telecom_ids.student.metric_note: Read `n_classes_predicted` before `macro_f1`. A linear student that stops predicting a class scores 0 on it by construction, and macro F1 then averages in a zero that looks like poor discrimination rather than an absent output - this repo's own QNN carries exactly that defect and is documented as doing so, so the check is not hypothetical. `agreement` is recorded but is NOT evidence the minority classes survived: agreement on the finance student rose from 0.884 to 0.947 across a change that left minority-class F1 unmoved, which is why per-class F1 is the headline here and the aggregate is a companion.
